bullets: Game 4 of a six-game single-deck session; only 124.8s readable (video 629.2-754.0), picked up at clock 2:45 against a Mortar/Rascals siege deck. Won by concession at clock 1:04.

The plan is X-Bow first, defend with the cheap cards: an early X-Bow at clock 2:36 on tile [2, 12] (left lane, three tiles off the river) took the enemy left tower from 4858 to 2790 by clock 2:14 while Berserker, Skeletons, Archers and Electro Spirit handled everything that came back.

Fireball is used offensively, not saved — clock 2:31 onto stacked Rascals at [12, 22] "just to get the pressure going really quickly" (t=644-646). Ryley calls the Fireball slot the reason the deck hard-counters Mortar (t=733-734).
Tesla appears once (clock 1:40, tile [4, 10]) purely as the screen beside a rebuilt X-Bow at [2, 12]; the deck defends mostly with troops and spends its building slot on the win condition.

The decisive habit is refusing to over-defend: at clock 1:12, with a rascal-boy already through, he takes 200 HP of chip and buys X-Bow (-6) plus Berserker (-2) instead — "it might be better to just eat some damage here and just go for an Expo plus Berserker push" (t=720-724). Enemy left tower goes 2734 -> 158 in eight seconds and the opponent quits.

Recurring theme across his commentary here: the X-Bow rework rewards a clean lock against decks without swarm cards and hits enemy siege buildings harder, though he is openly unsure whether it is a net buff (t=669-696).

new_deck.rationale: The X-Bow is the win condition and every other slot is cheap defence or cycle around it.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The list is X-Bow plus seven cards that are all 4 elixir or less, so the X-Bow can go down early and be rebuilt on cycle — Ryley plays it three times inside 90 readable seconds, always on tile [2, 12]. Defence is troop-based (Berserker, Skeletons, Archers, Electro Spirit) with Tesla reserved as a screen next to the siege building rather than as the primary answer, which keeps the elixir free to reload the win condition. Fireball is the swing card: cast offensively onto grouped support it both protects the lock and, as Ryley puts it, makes the deck "a hard counter against Mortar if I have the Fireball variation" (t=733-734). Because everything is cheap, the deck can afford to ignore a leaking attacker and answer with a fresh X-Bow plus Berserker instead — the exact trade that won this game.
